regime.title: 21 CFR Part 11 — electronic records and electronic signatures (US FDA)
regime.determination_by: the regulated organization, and the FDA on inspection

source.note: ecfr.gov, govinfo.gov and law.cornell.edu were unreachable when this map was written; clause numbers follow common citation and are unverified; requirement text is our paraphrase

rows.requirement: The system can tell an invalid or altered record from a good one.
rows.mechanism: Hash-chained, device-signed ledgers, checked by three implementations: Rust, JS, and a Python port of the JS math, held to the same verdicts by shared fixtures.
rows.limits: The host itself is out of scope (docs/root_paradox.md).

rows.requirement: The system is validated for its intended use.
rows.mechanism: The organization validates the system for its intended use. SecuraCV supplies the methodology and its test suites.
rows.operator_action: Validate the deployment for its intended use and keep the record.

rows.requirement: Accurate and complete copies of records can be produced in human-readable and electronic form for inspection.
rows.mechanism: export_events bundles; the court kit (verbatim bundle, digests, rendered custody record); render_human.
rows.limits: Events are bucketed claims; raw media is reachable only through break-glass.

rows.requirement: Records are protected so they can be accurately and readily retrieved throughout the retention period.
rows.mechanism: Receipt ledgers are never pruned. Retention deletes only sealed_events up to a checkpoint (src/storage.rs:786).
rows.operator_action: Set the retention period; back up the database and the high-water mark off-device.
rows.limits: Event records are deleted by retention by design.

rows.requirement: System access is limited to authorized individuals.
rows.mechanism: An n-of-m trustee quorum, re-derived at the gate, authorizes every disclosure; the API takes capability and paired tokens.

rows.requirement: System access is limited to authorized individuals.
rows.mechanism: Host and database access are the deployment's. There is no role model in the software.
rows.operator_action: Restrict host accounts, physical access and the database key.
rows.limits: No role-based access control exists in the software (tracked as Missing).

rows.requirement: Secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails record operator entries and actions without obscuring earlier entries.
rows.mechanism: Break-glass, export, policy-change and clock-provenance ledgers: append-only, hash-chained, device-signed; the named operator is recorded in break-glass and self-export context.
rows.limits: API exports name a credential class, not a person.

rows.requirement: Audit-trail entries carry the date and time of the action.
rows.mechanism: Audit-trail times are 10-minute buckets. Precise time exists only on anchoring acts (a TSA's genTime).
rows.reason: Sub-bucket times are never recorded, by design (Invariant III); whether bucket-level date and time is acceptable is the regulated organization's determination.

rows.requirement: Audit trails cannot be silently shortened.
rows.mechanism: An external signed high-water mark fails closed on tail truncation, rollback or wipe.
rows.operator_action: Set SECURACV_HWM_PATH on external media; without a configured high-water mark, tail truncation is not detected.

rows.requirement: Audit trails are protected against undetected alteration.
rows.mechanism: A Merkle tree and a signed checkpoint over every ledger.

rows.requirement: Audit trails are available for agency review and copying.
rows.mechanism: Periodic review of receipts, policy history and log_verify, recorded in the organization's record store.
rows.operator_action: Review on a cadence and record it (CPS 4.10).
rows.limits: A signed review attestation is the next row.

rows.requirement: Audit-trail review is itself recorded.
rows.mechanism: log_review attest: a reviewer-signed attestation through a tree size.

rows.requirement: Operational system checks enforce the permitted sequencing of steps and events.
rows.mechanism: The request hash is re-derived at the gate; the token is burned before decryption; the token is single use and replay is refused.

rows.requirement: Operational system checks enforce the permitted sequencing of steps and events.
rows.mechanism: Scripted ceremony steps enforced in order.

rows.requirement: Authority checks ensure only authorized individuals can use the system, sign a record or perform the operation at hand.
rows.mechanism: Quorum consent per request and per policy change; token-gated export.

rows.requirement: Device checks determine, as appropriate, the validity of the source of data input or operational instructions.
rows.mechanism: The organization validates its input devices and adapters. Each event records its input tier; that is a recorded label, not a validity check (capture_provenance map).
rows.operator_action: Validate cameras, adapters and bridges as part of system validation.
rows.limits: The kernel does not authenticate the camera.

rows.requirement: People who develop, maintain or use the system have the education, training and experience for their tasks.
rows.mechanism: A person must do this; the CPS records who holds which role.
rows.operator_action: Train the people who operate, approve and review.

rows.requirement: Written policies hold individuals accountable for actions taken under their electronic signatures.
rows.mechanism: A Custody Practice Statement template.
rows.operator_action: Adopt written accountability policies for actions taken under one's signature.

rows.requirement: System documentation is controlled in its distribution, access, use and revision.
rows.mechanism: Versioned docs in git; the kernel version in every kit's system description.
rows.operator_action: Control the revision and distribution of the deployment's own procedures.

rows.requirement: Open systems add controls such as encryption and digital signatures to protect records from their point of creation to their receipt.
rows.mechanism: Disclosure files carry Ed25519 signatures either way (11.70 row).
rows.operator_action: Determine whether the deployment is open or closed, and apply the added controls where it is open.

rows.requirement: Signed records show the signer's printed name, the date and time of signing, and the meaning of the signature.
rows.mechanism: render_human prints name, date/time and meaning.
rows.limits: Date/time is the 10-minute bucket; a trustee's printed name is the roster id.

rows.requirement: The name, date/time and meaning appear in every human-readable form of the record.
rows.mechanism: break_glass receipts --verbose prints the render_human record (requester, bucketed date/time, and each signature's meaning), with forged lines neutralized; the court kit's custody record names the authorizing grant by entry hash and its trustees by roster id.
rows.limits: The court kit's custody record does not use render_human: it names the grant and the trustees' roster ids but carries no per-signature meaning or date/time line. The full rendering is break_glass receipts --verbose on the producing database.

rows.requirement: Signatures are linked to their records so they cannot be removed, copied or transferred to falsify another record.
rows.mechanism: Per-domain signatures over entry and request hashes; approvals bound by approvals_commitment.

rows.requirement: Each electronic signature is unique to one individual and is not reused by or reassigned to anyone else.
rows.mechanism: One key per trustee; approvals are deduplicated by key.
rows.operator_action: One key per person, never shared or reassigned.

rows.requirement: The organization verifies an individual's identity before establishing or assigning an electronic signature.
rows.mechanism: Enrollment read-back in the runbook.
rows.operator_action: Verify identity before enrolling a trustee key.

rows.requirement: The organization verifies an individual's identity before establishing or assigning an electronic signature.
rows.mechanism: Enrollment attestation of hardware keys.

rows.requirement: Before use, the organization tells the agency in writing that its electronic signatures are intended as the legally binding equivalent of handwritten ones.
rows.mechanism: SecuraCV makes no statement to any agency.
rows.operator_action: Where the predicate rule calls for it, file the statement 11.100(c) describes.

rows.requirement: Non-biometric signatures use at least two distinct identification components and are used only by their genuine owners.
rows.mechanism: Passphrase-wrapped trustee keys and touch-gated hardware keys.
rows.limits: Today a trustee key file alone signs.

rows.requirement: Biometric signatures are designed so only their genuine owners can use them.
rows.mechanism: No biometric signature exists in SecuraCV.
rows.reason: Face and voice verification of trustees is rejected, ever; no biometric signature exists in SecuraCV.

rows.requirement: Identification codes and passwords are kept unique, checked periodically, and withdrawn when lost or compromised.
rows.mechanism: Revocation is a quorum policy change (spec/quorum_unseal_v2.md §3.1).
rows.operator_action: Revoke lost or departed keys through a policy change; review the roster periodically.

rows.requirement: Safeguards detect and report attempted unauthorized use, and devices that carry identification are tested periodically.
rows.mechanism: Grant notice and a single-trustee veto; enrollment attestation.
